 Oral Judgment

(PER: THE HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE ASHOK S. KINAGI)
1.

This appeal is filed by the insurance company challenging the judgment and award dated 30.01.2021 passed in MVC No.1112/2017 by the learned II Additional Sessions Judge and Member Additional MACT, Belagavi.
2. Brief facts leading rise to the filing of this appeal are as follows:
3. On 28.10.2015, when the deceased was riding a Hero Splendor motorcycle bearing registration No.KA.22/X.0101 from NC: 2026:KHC-D:3642 HC-KAR Belgavai towards Sambra and had reached near Ganesh Sweet Mart, Bellary nala, one unknown vehicle came from opposite direction and dashed against the said motorcycle.

sentences.text: The claimants are the legal representatives of deceased Manjunath.
They filed a claim petition under Section 163A of the MV Act seeking a compensation on account of the death of Manjunath in the road traffic accident.
Accordingly, prays to allow the claim petition.
4. Notice was issued to the owner of the Hero Honda Splendor.
Despite service of notice, he remained unrepresented.
The Tribunal placed him exparte.

5. Insurance company filed a statement of objections contending that the claim petition filed under Section 163A of the MV Act is not maintainable, as the deceased was earning more than  40,000/-
per annum and also contended that the deceased has violated Section 129 of MV Act.
Hence, on these grounds prays to dismiss the claim petition.
NC: 2026:KHC-D:3642 HC-KAR 6.
The Tribunal based on the pleadings of the parties framed the relevant issues.
7. The petitioners to substantiate their case, Petitioner No.1 was examined as PW1 and marked 8 documents Exhibit P1 to Exhibit P8.

In rebuttal, the insurance company examined its officer as RW.1 and marked two documents as Exhibit R1 and R2.
8.

The tribunal, after assessing the verbal and documentary evidence, allowed the claim petition in part with costs and awarded a compensation of  9,80,000/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of claim petition till realisation of the entire award amount and directed the respondent insurance company to deposit the said amount together with accrued interest.
9. The insurance company aggrieved by the impugned judgment, filed this miscellaneous first appeal.

10. Heard the arguments of the learned counsel for the insurance company and learned counsel for the claimants.
NC: 2026:KHC-D:3642 HC-KAR 11.
The learned counsel for the insurance company submit that the deceased was riding the vehicle which belongs to his father.
Hence, the claimants cannot maintain a claim petition under Section 163A of the Act and he submits that the deceased steps into the shoes of the insurer.
Hence, the Insurance company is not liable to indemnify the insurer.
He also submitted that the deceased was an engineer and earning more than 40,000/- per annum.

Hence, the claim petition under Section 163A of the MV Act is not maintainable and to buttress his argument he has placed a reliance on the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of New India Assurance Company v. Sadanand Mukhi and others reported in 2009 (1) TAC 425 (S.C.) and Deepal Girishbhai Soni and others v.
United India Insurance Company reported in 2004 ACJ 934.

sentences.text: Per contra, learned counsel for the claimants submits that in case if the court comes to a conclusion that the claimants are not entitled for compensation, she submits that the claimants are entitled to a sum of Rs.1,00,000/-, as there is a contract between the insurer and the insurance company to pay the NC: 2026:KHC-D:3642 HC-KAR compensation amount to the extent of 1,00,000/-.

To buttress her arguments, she has placed reliance on the judgment of Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Ramkhiladi and others v. United India Insurance Co. Ltd. and others reported in AIR 2020 SC 527.

entities.text: Ramkhiladi and others v. United India Insurance Co. Ltd. and others reported in AIR 2020 SC 527
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence, on this ground she prays to dispose of the appeal.

13. Perused the records and considered the submissions of the learned counsel for the parties.
14.
The point that would arise for consideration is regarding the quantum of compensation.
15. It is an undisputed fact that the deceased Manjunath was riding the motorcycle on 20.10.2015 and he met with an accident and sustained injuries and succumbed to the injuries on 15.11.2015.
The claimants being the legal representatives of the deceased, filed a claim petition under Section 163A of the MV Act claiming compensation.
Admittedly, the deceased Manjunath was an Engineer and earning more than Rs.40,000/- annually.
16. As rightly contented by the learned counsel for the insurance company, the petition filed under Section 163A of MV NC: 2026:KHC-D:3642 HC-KAR Act is not maintainable.

However, from the perusal of the policy, it clearly discloses that the insurer is entitled for a sum of 1,00,000/- in view of the contract between the insurer and the insurance company and the claimants, at the most, are entitled for a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- under the personal accident.
In view of the proposition of law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in case of Ramkhiladi (supra), the deceased steps into the shoes of the owner of the vehicle.
The claimatns cannot claim compensation against the insurance company of the said motorcycle.
However, in the instant case, as per the contract of insurance, the owner cum driver was entitled to a sum of Rs.1,00,000/-.
The said aspect was not considered by the Tribunal and committed an error in awarding a compensation of Rs.9,80,000/-.
The impugned judgment passed by the Tribunal awarding Rs.9,80,000/- is arbitrary and erroneous.
17. For the foregoing reasons, the point is answered accordingly.

18. In view of the above discussion, I proceed to pass the following:
NC: 2026:KHC-D:3642 HC-KAR ORDER i.
The appeal is allowed in part.
ii. The judgment and award dated 30.01.2021 passed in MVC No.1112 of 2017 by the learned II Additional Sessions Judge and Member of Addl. MACT, Belagavi, is modified.
The claimants are entitled for a sum of Rs.1,00,000/-, as per the contract, with interest at the rate of 9% per annum from the date of petition till realisation.
iii. The insurance company shall deposit the said amount within six weeks from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment.
The Registry is directed to transmit the amount in deposit and the TCR to the Tribunal forthwith.
